issues.sym: Check engine light (often misfire codes), rough idle, misfires, weak power, hard starting or oil burning.
issues.why: Valve seats in the cylinder head on these early engines wear out too soon, so valves stop sealing and compression drops. GM extended coverage on this repair years ago, but that window has closed.
issues.next: Have a compression or leak-down test done soon. A flashing check engine light means ease off and get it in right away, since it can ruin the catalytic converter. The usual fix is an updated cylinder head.

issues.sym: Engine revs flare on the 2-3 shift, third and fourth gears slip or disappear, and the fluid may smell burnt or look dark.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic's 3-4 clutch pack burns up when pressure in that circuit drops, often worsened by heat, towing and old fluid.
issues.next: Get a fluid check and road test soon and avoid towing. Driving on a slipping transmission usually turns a rebuild into a replacement.

issues.t: Blower fan quits or only works on some speeds
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan stops working, or only runs on certain settings, so the defroster may not clear the windshield.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor behind the glove box fails early, often because an aging blower motor draws too much current.
issues.next: Have the blower motor tested along with the resistor, otherwise a new resistor can fail again. Fix it before winter so the defroster works.

issues.sym: A check engine light or fuel cap message with the truck running normally, sometimes a fuel smell.
issues.why: A worn gas cap that does not seal or a sticking EVAP vent valve lets the evaporative system fail its leak test.
issues.next: Make sure the cap clicks tight, or try a new cap. If the light returns, have the codes read and the vent valve checked.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power steering assist (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly turns heavy, mostly at low speed, with a power steering warning on the dash.
issues.why: A poor electrical connection at the steering gear connector can cut the electric assist. GM recalled affected trucks and later issued a follow-up recall.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free repair. Allow extra steering effort until then.

issues.t: Driver front airbag may deploy improperly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning beforehand. The problem shows up only in a serious crash.
issues.why: The driver airbag may not inflate correctly during its second stage in a high-speed crash. GM recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done promptly.

issues.sym: A rumble-strip vibration at steady speeds under light throttle, sometimes with jerky or harsh shifts.
issues.why: The torque converter clutch shudders with the original fluid. GM's bulletin fix is a full fluid exchange with updated fluid.
issues.next: Ask a Chevrolet dealer about bulletin 18-NA-355. Get it done before the shudder wears the torque converter.

issues.t: Diesel warnings and no-starts from chafed engine wiring
issues.sym: Several warning lights at once, DEF or check engine messages, an oil pressure gauge that jumps around, misfire, rough running or crank-no-start.
issues.why: The engine wiring harness or its connectors can rub through and short. GM issued a bulletin on finding and repairing the chafed spots.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the codes and inspect the harness per bulletin 22-NA-003 before replacing sensors.

issues.t: DEF fault on cold starts (emissions recall)
issues.sym: A DEF warning and a speed-will-be-limited message after starting in freezing weather.
issues.why: The DEF pump can switch on before frozen fluid has thawed, so the system logs a fault and stops dosing for that drive. GM issued an emissions recall to reprogram the engine computer.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the software update. Do not ignore DEF warnings, since the truck can limit its speed.

issues.t: Turbo engine wiring chafes on hot parts
issues.sym: Check engine light with injector or misfire codes, a Reduced Power message, ABS or several other warnings, or a no-start.
issues.why: The engine wiring harness can rub against the turbo heat shield or wastegate linkage and wear through. GM issued bulletins on rerouting and repairing it.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the harness near the turbo per bulletins PIE0808 or PIP6062 before swapping injectors or sensors.

issues.sym: Low coolant warnings, coolant puddles or a sweet smell, a check engine light, and in bad cases overheating.
issues.why: The quick-connect fittings on the radiator hoses can leak early in the truck's life. GM opened a special coverage program for this.
issues.next: Do not keep driving if the temperature climbs or a low coolant warning appears. Ask a Chevrolet dealer about special coverage N262546590.

issues.t: Ticking from the top of the engine
issues.sym: A steady ticking or tapping from the top of the engine that follows engine speed.
issues.why: Debris from manufacturing can lodge in a hydraulic lash adjuster in the valvetrain so it goes soft and ticks. GM issued a bulletin to replace the soft adjusters and their rocker arms.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the source under warranty and ask about bulletin PIP6101. Avoid high revs until it is repaired.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking activates for no reason (recall)
issues.sym: The truck brakes hard by itself on a clear road, sometimes with a forward collision alert.
issues.why: The front camera module can falsely detect an obstacle. GM recalled affected trucks for a software fix.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the update promptly.

issues.t: Front wheel hub bolts may loosen or break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or wobble from a front wheel, or a steering vibration that gets worse with speed.
issues.why: Hub bolts were over-tightened and damaged at the factory, so they can loosen or snap. GM recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you feel a clunk or wobble from a front wheel, stop driving and have it towed in.

issues.t: Fuel pump lock ring not fully secured (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing. Some owners may notice a fuel smell near the tank.
issues.why: The ring that holds the fuel pump module in the tank may not have been fully locked at the factory, which could let fuel leak, especially in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you smell fuel, do not drive it and have it inspected.
